gen-gf-unkempt-gf-m-plus-2: M PLUS 2 reads friendly and businesslike, its gaping c leaving the letters easy to tell apart. Unkempt is the one to catch the eye with its sturdy t, and M PLUS 2 does the quiet work of carrying the words.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-m-plus-code-latin: Approachable and tidy, with a bit of a swagger up top. Unkempt brings the shouty energy while M PLUS Code Latin, bent like neon tubing, keeps every sans letter open-mouthed and friendly.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: M PLUS Rounded 1c reads soft and unfussy, its terminals stopping short instead of curling back in on themselves. Paragraphs of it would go down smoothly.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-mandali: Unkempt looks brushed on by a sign painter, one stroke at constant width. Mandali follows in quiet sans-serif, its generous entry into the e making a long page go down gently.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-manjari: Manjari curves with wide, unclosed terminals and a line that never wavers in weight. Unkempt then adds the loud, hand-built headline voice, while Manjari keeps the sans-serif text steady underneath.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-meera-inimai: Unkempt has a commanding, hand-made look, its t carrying crossbar and stem in matching weight. Meera Inimai suits a modest size, where its open curves can breathe.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-mina: Unkempt shouts with an expressive, hand-drawn confidence, every t built from matching strokes. Mina, thin as stitched thread, stays out of its way.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-mingzat: Mingzat has curvy, unclamped letters that feel modern and businesslike, flowing in a low-contrast sans line. Against Unkempt's heavy, single-weight rounds and stems, that softness is the pair's strongest pull.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-moderustic: Rough, loud and laser-etched in feel, Unkempt traces each letter at constant width. Moderustic answers in a modern sans-serif, its broad-nib curves left open and unfinished.
gen-gf-unkempt-gf-molengo: Unkempt draws with near-zero stroke contrast, hand-built and commanding, with gaps that stop c turning into o. Molengo takes over below in sans-serif, its wide gaps keeping tiny sizes crisp.
